summary: Redwood reviewed data residency and region-pinning options for Aurea HealthTech. topics: Data residency and region pinning options
SOC 2 / ISO attestations and audit logs
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Jenna (Aurea - CISO): Jenna here.
[00:11] Liam (Aurea - Head of Platform): Liam here.
[00:13] Priya (Aurea - Cloud Security): Priya here.
[00:15] Marcus (Redwood SE): Marcus here.
[00:18] Sofia: Great. We're here to walk through data residency, region pinning, and your compliance checklist. We'll go through high-level controls and then Marcus can take a technical deep dive.
[00:34] Jenna: Perfect, thanks. Quick context: Aurea is regulated in the EU and US, a lot of PHI-adjacent data flows. Main asks are: can you guarantee EU-only processing and logs, how do you handle cross-border fallbacks, what's the subprocessor list, and key management (BYOK) options? Also need SOC2 and ISO paperwork.
[01:05] Sofia: Totally understood. On the paperwork side we can share SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate — we'll attach those after the call. For residency, we support region pinning at the tenant level and per-route options depending on deployment. Marcus?
[01:22] Marcus: Yeah, to add — there are three common modes: Hosted (multi-region), Dedicated (reserved capacity in a specific region), and Private (VPC or on-prem). For strict EU-only processing we recommend Dedicated in eu-west-1 or Private VPC deployed in the customer's region. Hosted can be configured with EU-only routing but has more complex fallback behaviors.
[01:45] Jenna: When you say "fallback behaviors" — if eu-west-1 has an outage, will requests go to the US? That's a hard no for our legal team unless we've got explicit consent and SCCs in place.
[01:58] Marcus: Good callout. By default hosted will fall back to a compatible regional pool if the primary region is unhealthy. But for customers requiring hard pinning, we offer hard region pinning for Dedicated and Private where cross-border routing is disabled at the routing layer. For Hosted we can set policies that avoid cross-border fallback, but it removes automatic high-availability across regions — you can configure regional failover windows and manual failover processes.
[02:27] Priya: Do you have contractual guarantees — like in the DPA — that prohibit cross-border processing, or is that a best-effort config?
[02:35] Sofia: We include region pinning options in the DPA and we can add explicit clauses for EU-only processing. That said, we also include standard SCCs for cross-border transfers and can sign additional addenda if needed. We'll send a draft.
[02:49] Liam: Subprocessors — who exactly touches the data? We need an up-to-date list including cloud infra and any logging/monitoring vendors.
[02:58] Marcus: Sure. Primary subprocessors are the cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure depending on region), our logging provider for aggregated telemetry, and a small number of managed database vendors for metadata. I'll send the full list. Important note: for Private deployments you control the infra and subprocessors are minimized. For Dedicated we can also minimize third-party access and isolate storage in your region.
[03:26] Jenna: We saw notes in your docs about audit logs — where are audit logs stored, and can they be pinned to EU region?
[03:35] Marcus: Audit logs for tenant activity can be stored in-region. For Hosted, logs are by default stored in the region serving the requests but some aggregated telemetry may be exported to our analytics platform — we can configure retention and toggle exports. For Dedicated and Private we offer full control to keep logs in-region and disable external exports.
[03:56] Priya: Encryption — do you support customer-managed keys? We require KMS with BYOK and ideally HSM-backed keys.
[04:04] Sofia: Yes, we support customer-managed keys. Marcus to explain the options: BYOK via cloud KMS (customer project), or bring-your-own-HSM in Private deployments.
[04:14] Marcus: Right. Options: 1) Hosted with CMK — you provide keys in your cloud project and we use them for encrypting stored artifacts. 2) Dedicated with CMK + restricted key access so only the serving runtime can call KMS. 3) Private on-prem where you hold keys entirely. We also support envelope encryption and double-encrypt patterns if you need an extra layer. Note, some telemetry and ephemeral caches don't persist to disk, but persistent artifacts (model cache, logs, KV caches persisted to storage) can be encrypted with your CMK.
[04:46] Jenna: How about access to keys — does Redwood ever have access or copy of the plaintext keys?
[04:51] Marcus: No, not for BYOK. We only get the CMK references and permissions to use the key via IAM roles. We don't export key material. For HSM deployments, the customer retains the key material.
[05:04] Priya: OK. For legal — Schrems II and adequacy decisions, we need SCCs and confirmation no subprocessor outside EEA will access EU personal data.
[05:13] Sofia: We'll include SCCs in the DPA. For subprocessors outside the EEA we can document the access controls and admin-level access strictly limited; for strict no-cross-border access we'd recommend Dedicated pinned in EU or Private.
[05:26] Jenna: Can you give a concrete example: say a user in Paris hits our app, the request should be processed and tokens persisted only in eu-west-1 — logs and any backups also stored in eu-west-1. If your primary pool goes down, we want request failure rather than failover to US. Is that achievable?
[05:44] Marcus: Yes — with Dedicated hard-pin you can enforce failure rather than cross-region failover. Hosted can be configured similarly but it's not the default; we'll need to change routing policies and accept the availability trade-off.
[05:58] Liam: Monitoring — what about support for on-prem SIEM integration, e.g., send logs to our Splunk located in eu-west-1?
[06:07] Marcus: We have structured audit logs and event exporters. For Dedicated/Private we can push logs to your Splunk endpoint inside your VPC or S3 in eu-west-1. For Hosted we can set up push endpoints but you'll want to confirm network egress and where the collector lives.
[06:22] Priya: RBAC and SAML — can we integrate SSO and SCIM for provisioning and ensure least privilege?
[06:29] Sofia: Yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is configurable per-tenant with roles tied to SAML groups; audit trails show admin actions.
[06:39] Jenna: On audit trails — are they tamper-evident? We need a chain of custody for admin actions and key rotation history.
[06:47] Marcus: Audit logs are append-only in our system; we can store immutable logs in WORM-backed S3 buckets in-region for Dedicated. For Hosted we have similar controls but we'd need to map retention/immutability to your requirements. Key rotation events are logged, and we can produce exportable logs for quarterly audits.
[07:07] Sonia (background noise — speaker mislabel): [inaudible]
[07:12] Sofia: Sorry, who was that?
[07:14] Jenna: No, that's fine, ignore.
[07:16] Sofia: A couple of practical items: We'll share the SOC 2 Type II and ISO certs and the subprocessor list after this call. Marcus will prepare a data flow diagram showing where data lands in eu-west-1 and what components might touch it.
[07:31] Liam: For the EU pilot — what SLA and support model are you proposing? We need 99.9 for latency-sensitive endpoints and PD for incident response.
[07:40] Sofia: For Dedicated we can commit to 99.9 uptime for the serving pool and provide an assigned CSM and dedicated infra slack channel. For Hosted EU-only with no failover the SLA would be similar but with caveats around cross-region availability; we can put these in the contract.
[07:58] Priya: One more question on data retention — can we set per-tenant retention windows, auto-delete model cache after X days, and exclude certain data from logging?
[08:08] Marcus: Yes. Retention policies are configurable: you can set TTLs for caches and model artifacts, and redact or disable application-level logging of prompt/response content. Some operational logs (errors, system telemetry) remain but can be configured to exclude PII.
[08:25] Jenna: Regarding sub-processors — do you have a process for notifying customers of changes? We need 30 days notice for any subprocessor that will process EU personal data.
[08:34] Sofia: Standard process is 30 days for major subprocessor changes; we'll include that in the DPA. We also do an annual audit of subprocessors.
[08:42] Priya: For the pilot, we want to test BYOK integration with our KMS. Is there a sandbox flow?
[08:49] Marcus: Yes, we have a sandbox deployment pattern where you can bring keys in a dev project. For the pilot we'll set up a Dedicated test instance in eu-west-1 with your CMKs and we can validate end-to-end.
[09:01] Liam: Are there any limitations on model caching or performance with CMK usage? Sometimes KMS requests add latency.
[09:08] Marcus: Good question. We use envelope encryption to avoid per-request KMS calls for inference; the runtime holds data keys in memory and only the key-encryption-key is used to unwrap/persist. So minimal latency impact. For cache misses that require decrypt, there's a small overhead but not per-token.
[09:27] Jenna: Can we get a list of the specific AWS/GCP regions and endpoints you'll use for EU residency? We need to map to our allowlist firewall rules.
[09:35] Sofia: Yep — Marcus will send a complete allowlist of endpoints and IP ranges for eu-west-1 and any required control plane endpoints.
[09:44] Priya: What about backups and DR — are backups stored in-region? And how long are they retained?
[09:50] Marcus: Backups for Dedicated can be set to in-region only with configurable retention; we'll mirror your retention policy for the pilot. For Hosted we have cross-region backups by default but can opt-out for EU-only customers. We'll document backup lifecycle in the DPA.
[10:08] Jenna: Regarding certifications — are you willing to sign a right-to-audit clause? Our procurement usually wants that for vendors handling regulated data.
[10:16] Sofia: We do include right-to-audit clauses but typically they are scoped — we provide audit evidence (SOC 2 reports, penetration test summaries) and GA/attestation; in-person audits are handled case-by-case. We'll surface standard language in the contract.
[10:28] Marcus: One nuance — for Hosted customers we collect some anonymized telemetry for platform health; that telemetry doesn't include PII and can be disabled for EU-only tenancy if required.
[10:40] Liam: Any recommendations for minimizing risk during ramp? We want to avoid mixing EU and US data in analytics buckets.
[10:47] Marcus: Best practice: start with Dedicated EU tenant, pin region, configure CMK, disable aggregated analytics export, set retention policies, and use VPC peering for log ingestion to your Splunk. That gives minimal subprocessors and maximum control.
[11:02] Jenna: OK great. Let's recap next steps.
[11:06] Sofia: Recap — we'll send SOC2 and ISO certs, subprocessor list, sample DPA with SCCs, and an allowlist of endpoints. Marcus will prepare a data flow diagram and draft pilot plan for Dedicated eu-west-1 with BYOK. You'll provide sample datasets and compliance questions.
[11:23] Priya: Sounds good. ETA on docs?
[11:26] Sofia: SOC2/ISO and subprocessor list by 2026-06-11, data flow and allowlist by 2026-06-12, pilot scoping doc by 2026-06-15.
[11:34] Jenna: Fine. We'll review and schedule the technical deep dive.
[11:36] Marcus: Happy to do the deep dive — we can walk through key rotation flows, KMS IAM roles, and the encrypted runtime design.
[11:45] Sofia: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email and link the docs.
[11:49] Jenna: Thanks.
[11:50] Liam: Thanks all.
[11:52] Priya: Bye.
[11:55] Sofia: Bye.
